chunks: Abu Ja'far al-Mansur wrote to Muhammad ibn Khalid — who was his governor over Medina — that he should ask the people of Medina about the five from two hundred in zakat, how it came to be the weight of seven, and this was not the case in the era of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). He instructed him that among those he asks should be Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: He asked the people of Medina, and they said: 'We found those who were before us upon this.'

So he sent for Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He asked Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and he said the same as the jurists of the people of Medina. Then he said: 'What do you say, O Abu Abdillah?' He said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) assigned one uqiyya in every forty uqiyyas. When you calculate that, it comes out to the weight of seven — and it had been the weight of six, and the dirham was five dawaniqs.'

Habib said: We calculated it and found it to be exactly as he had said. So Abdullah ibn al-Hasan turned to him and said: 'From where did you take this?' He said: 'I read it in the Book of your mother Fatima.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent back: 'I only informed you that I had read it; I did not inform you that it is with me.' Habib said: Muhammad ibn Khalid kept saying to me, 'I have never seen the likes of this!'

key_terms.الأوقية: Uqiyya — a unit of weight equal to forty dirhams
key_terms.الدوانيق: Dawaniqs (pl. of daniق) — a unit of weight, one-sixth of a dirham; five dawaniqs = five-sixths of a dirham
key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — obligatory almsgiving, one of the pillars of Islam
key_terms.كتاب فاطمة: The Book of Fatima — a sacred text passed down among the Imams, distinct from the Quran

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the zakat weight calculation and the Book of Fatima?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the official Abbasid inquiry about zakat weights, explaining that the Prophet (SAWW) set zakat at one uqiyya per forty, which — given the historical dirham weight of five dawaniqs — equates to a weight of seven. When pressed by Abdullah ibn al-Hasan about his source, the Imam revealed he had read it in the Book of Fatima, a sacred written legacy of Lady Fatima al-Zahra (AS). The Imam's careful refusal to loan the book — noting he had read it but not that it was in his possession — illustrates his wisdom and the special status of that scripture.
